findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: There was an accumulation of a pink substance on the outer baffles of the ice machine in the new kitchen space. Shown to the PIC and the baffles were cleaned and sanitized during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that baffles of the ice machine are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed a 1/2 gallon of fat free milk to exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date (in cafe area). The use-by-date was 11/6/2024 and was stored in a mini cooler across from the cash register. Discussed with PIC and the milk was discarded. Ensure that milks stored in house longer than 24 hours are date marked and never exceed the manufacturer’s use by date. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw shell eggs stored above ready-to-eat foods (produce, cake pops, yogurt,  in coolers in both the main cafe and the Express cafe. CORRECTED- Discussed proper storage with PICs, who will rearrange storage to keep eggs on the lowest shelf. Store raw shell eggs below anything ready-to-eat.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Mold observed on the baffles of ice machines in both the main cafe and the Express cafe. Clean baffles regularly so that they are clean to sight and touch.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
No sanitizer buckets made

750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

Corrected Immediately

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed the scoop handle in the hot chocolate powder to be stored in contact with the powder. Make sure to store scoop handles with the handle extended up and out of the food. 
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed a set of tongs on the table in front of the sandwich press machines to have melted and cracked plastic coating on the food contact portion of the tongs. Food contact surfaces must be free from unnecessary crevices that would impede effective cleaning. Replace tongs.
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
Observed the thermometer gauge on the final rinse side of the dish machine to be reading at 210F and to not move during multiple cycles run on the machine when a thermometer run through the dish machine itself read a maximum temperature of 152F. Thermometer must be accurate to =/- 3 degrees F. Repair thermometer gauge.
750-830c A thermometer ±3°F shall be provided to check the temperature of  the water in each tank of the dish machine and the temperature of  the final rinse water as it enters the manifold.

findings.title: Sanitizing temperature
findings.comment:
Observed the final rinse on the dish machine to only be reaching 152F maximum according to a calibrated digital maximum registering thermometer that was run through the dish machine twice and that a thermolabel run through the dish machine on a metal ice scoop did not change color to indicate that the scoop had reached 160F. A call was placed to have the machine serviced and in the meantime, the facility will use the dish facilities in the adjacent school in order to wash, rinse and sanitize all dishware. 
750-830 All hot water for sanitizing dishes and equipment must be a minimum of 180F when it leaves the dish washing machine manifold in order to kill pathogens.  Properly sanitize all items. Check and maintain the dishwasher frequently.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the front panel on the ice machine to not be attached. Re-attach panel to the front of the ice machine.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floors in the cafe area to have food debris underneath equipment. Clean the floors. Janitorial staff sweeps after daily use and mops weekly on Saturdays. It was discussed to request that they ensure that floors underneath equipment are addressed as well.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed an accumulation of dust and debris on floors under the cabinets and equipment throughout the facility. Clean the floors.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
